「四物」字面上就是「四件樂器」，指的是꽹과리（kkwaenggwari，小鑼）、: "Samul" means literally "four things", and it refers to 꽹과리 (kkwaenggwari, the small gong), 징 (jing, the gong), 장구 (janggu, the hourglass drum) and 북 (buk, the drum). This is not rhetoric but the definition of the line-up: these four make up the core, and any other instrument is an addition.
一隊人打著鼓、跳著舞、舉著旗，沿著村路移動；另一群人在舞台上站立演奏，只靠四件樂: One group walks along a village road, drumming, dancing and carrying flags; another stands on a stage and plays the same set of rhythms with only four instruments. The first is pungmul (풍물 / 농악), the second is samul nori (사물놀이), and together they make up the Korean tradition of samul nori and pungmul. They share four instruments — small gong, gong, hourglass drum and drum — but one serves ritual and procession, the other serves the concert.
伴奏型是循環的、可預期的；訊號則是短的、跳出循環的樂句，通常由小鑼或太平簫發出，: The accompaniment patterns are cyclical and predictable; signals are short phrases that step out of the cycle, usually given by the small gong or the taepyeongso, with the whole group following. The call-and-response structure of pungmul is plain: the sangsoe (leader) proposes, the busoe (second) answers, then everyone joins. This pattern of "question, answer, then all together" appears at every change of section.
低音、單純、不花俏。打出最基本的拍點，讓所有人在密集的聲音裡仍踩得到地: Low, plain, unadorned. It plays the most basic beats so that everyone can still feel the ground under a dense texture
先鎖定小鑼。它的聲音最尖，是整隊的神經中樞；聽它什麼時候變密、什麼時候停。: Fix first on the small gong. Its sound is the sharpest and it is the nerve centre of the group; listen for when it thickens and when it stops.
再聽鉦。它打得少，但每一響都決定段落的邊界。試著數一段音樂裡鉦響了幾次。: Then the gong. It is struck seldom, but every stroke decides where a section ends. Try counting how many times the gong sounds in one stretch of music.
和中國鑼鼓相比，差別在領導者用什麼下命令。鑼鼓的板鼓手用鼓棒指揮，其他人不看彼此: Compared with Chinese luogu, the difference is what the leader uses to give orders. The luogu ban drummer conducts with a stick, the others never look at each other but only at the stick, and a whole pattern can be remembered as the spoken syllables of the luogu jing; in samul nori and pungmul the leader is himself a player, the gong's sound is music and command at once, and the patterns are held through the body, through spoken syllables (쿵, 짝, 덩, 덕 and so on) and through familiarity, never developing into a complete spoken notation as the luogu jing did.
和日本太鼓團相比，兩者都沒有指揮、都靠鼓聲分層，差別在領導是否集中在一人身上。四: Compared with a Japanese taiko group, neither has a conductor and both layer the sound through drums; the difference is whether leadership is concentrated in one person. The small-gong player in samul nori and pungmul is an explicit leader, his gong sharp and penetrating and used specifically for giving orders, and the others watch him; a taiko group has no such role, and its time is spread across the base rhythm of the shime-daiko, the visual signals of the sticks and the stops of the whole ensemble.
和韓國國樂管弦樂團相比，差別在編制邏輯。後者有指揮、有總譜、把傳統樂器擴充成高音: Compared with the Korean gugak orchestra, the difference is the logic of the line-up. The latter has a conductor and a full score, and expands traditional instruments into a family running from treble to bass; samul nori's core is four percussion instruments with no dedicated conductor, and its unit of music is a set of named rhythm patterns rather than a written score.
四物就是四件樂器：小鑼、鉦、杖鼓、鼓。名稱直接說明了核心編制，其他樂器是外加的。: The four things are four instruments: small gong, gong, hourglass drum, drum. The name states the core line-up directly, and any other instrument is an addition. It means what it says; it is not a metaphor.
四物農樂的「四物」是指四種場合或四個段落。: The "four things" of samul nori and pungmul are four occasions, or four sections.
四物놀이 則屬於劇場與國際巡演。它在二十世紀後半成形，把風物中的節奏抽出、重新排: Samul nori, by contrast, belongs to the theatre and to international touring. It took shape in the second half of the twentieth century, drawing the rhythms out of pungmul and rearranging them into stage-length pieces, and from then on made "samul" the name of a genre. Today in Korea and abroad many school clubs and amateur groups learn both forms at once: pungmul teaches formation, ritual and movement, samul nori teaches sections, solos and stage direction.
它拿掉小鼓、太平簫、旗與舞者，只留四件樂器，把風物中長時間的循環剪成幾分鐘的段落: It removes the sogo, the taepyeongso, the flags and the dancers, keeps only four instruments, cuts the long cycles of pungmul into segments of a few minutes, and arranges an order for the stage: usually a slow, long pattern to begin, a gradual speeding up, a janggu solo inserted, and the densest pattern to close. Without the procession and the ritual, control of time moves from the footsteps to the understanding between players; the small gong is still the leader, but what it leads has changed from "where we walk" to "when we change section".
它的兩面是兩種語言：低音面是「重量」，高音面是「細節」。傳統上左手拍低音面、右手: Its two faces are two languages: the bass face is "weight", the treble face is "detail". Traditionally the left hand strikes the bass face and the right hand holds a bamboo stick for the treble face, and the alternation of the two builds the pattern. In samul nori the janggu often has a solo passage of its own (설장구, seoljanggu), starting from a slow pattern, growing denser, and finally rejoining the group. The solo is not only display: it plays the whole rhythmic system in miniature, first the skeleton, then the decoration.
它的型最簡單，幾乎不變，音量沉在底下。鼓手在風物裡通常使用一根鼓棒（북채）擊打鼓: Its pattern is the simplest and hardly changes, and its volume sits underneath. In pungmul the drummer usually uses a single stick (북채, bukchae) on the head, crouching low and moving large; the sound has none of the janggu's detail, but it is the body weight of the group. When the procession moves and footsteps and crowd noise mix in, the drum is the one part that lets everyone confirm they are still on the same beat.
它的聲音尖而短，能穿過鼓聲、人聲與戶外的風，所以它適合下指令。持小鑼的상쇠不只打: Its sound is sharp and short, cutting through drums, voices and the outdoor wind, which is why it suits giving orders. The sangsoe who holds the small gong does more than keep time: he changes the density of the group with gestures, decides with the angle of his body where the procession goes, and marks a section with a sudden raise of the gong or a shout. The others' attention is in fact always on the small gong, not on their own drums. This division — "listen to your own hands, watch someone else's gong" — is why pungmul can stay together while moving.
它音量最大、餘韻最長，但打得最少。它的工作是「讓時間停下來」：在一個密集的段落之: It is the loudest and has the longest decay, yet it is struck the least. Its work is to stop time: after a dense section one stroke of the gong pushes the sound aside so the next section has room to begin. The gong player usually stands at a fixed point in the procession, controlling the breathing of the whole piece with very few strokes. Listen to pungmul attending only to the drums and the rhythm feels busy; take the gong in and you find plenty of blank space between the busy sections.
小鑼是這套系統的大腦。: The small gong is the brain of this system.
找有隊伍移動的影片。看腳步與重拍的關係，比聽錄音更能理解風物。: Look for videos where the group is moving. Seeing how the footsteps sit against the strong beat teaches you more about pungmul than any recording.
曲目上，兩者共用的是一組節奏型的名字，而不是一首首寫定的曲子。同一個型可以在不同: In repertoire the two share a set of names for rhythm patterns, not a list of fixed pieces. The same pattern can appear on different occasions and at different lengths; what changes is the number of repetitions and the ornaments, not the skeleton.
杖鼓負責把話說清楚。: The janggu is what makes the sentence clear.
每個段落都有固定的節奏型與轉換訊號，即興發生在型的內部。正因為骨架固定，十幾個人: Every section has a fixed rhythm pattern and a signal for changing to the next, and improvisation happens inside the pattern. Because the skeleton is fixed, a dozen people can play at once without falling apart.
比較風物與四物놀이 的同一段節奏：前者鬆、長、有空間，後者緊、短、段落分明。: Compare the same stretch of rhythm in pungmul and in samul nori: the first is loose, long and roomy, the second tight, short and clearly divided into sections.
沙漏形鼓，左手拍低音面、右手以竹枝擊高音面。它打出完整的節奏型（장단），是把拍子: An hourglass-shaped drum; the left hand strikes the bass face and the right hand beats the treble face with a bamboo stick. It plays the complete rhythm pattern (장단, jangdan) and is the instrument that states the beat clearly
注意杖鼓的兩面：低音面與高音面交替，形成整個節奏的骨架。: Watch the two faces of the janggu: bass face and treble face alternate and form the skeleton of the whole rhythm.
為什麼是這四件？因為它們把「時間」拆成四個不同的解析度：鼓給你地板，杖鼓給你句子: Why these four? Because they cut "time" into four different resolutions: the drum gives you the floor, the janggu gives you sentences, the gong gives you sections, the small gong gives you orders. Once the four layers are separated, even if one is scattered by the wind or blocked by the crowd, the other three still hold.
移動是風物的常態，不是例外。: Moving is the normal state of pungmul, not the exception.
訊號與伴奏的分界，靠的是長度與位置。: The line between signal and accompaniment comes down to length and position.
這種音樂全靠鼓手即興，沒有固定結構。: This music is all improvisation by the drummers, with no fixed structure.
鉦的功能與直覺相反。: The gong's function is the opposite of what you would expect.
隊伍一邊走一邊打，樂器掛在身上，腳步與拍點必須對得上。所以風物的節奏型通常與步伐: The group plays while it walks, the instruments are strapped on, and the steps have to line up with the beats. So pungmul patterns are usually tied to the step: which foot the strong beat falls on decides whether the procession can move in unison. For a performance in one spot the group forms a set shape (five directions, for instance), and the music switches from travelling to standing, density and tempo changing with it. The small gong's signal starts the switch: the whole group stops at the same instant, takes its stand and enters the next pattern.
韓國四物農樂（Samul Nori and Pungmul）— 以小鑼領奏的四件: Samul Nori and Pungmul — a four-instrument percussion line-up led by the small gong, Korean festival drumming that moved from village processions into the concert hall. Ensembles and instrumentation by Next Door Sound Weavers.
韓國四物農樂｜合奏與編制百科: Samul Nori and Pungmul | Ensembles and instrumentation
音最低、餘韻最長。通常只敲少數幾個點，標記樂句的結束與段落的轉彎，給整個節奏「空: Lowest in pitch, longest in decay. It usually strikes only a few points, marking the ends of phrases and the turns of sections, and gives the whole rhythm its "space"
音最高、最尖、最穿透。持者（상쇠，sangsoe）用敲擊、手勢、眼神與喊聲帶領全: Highest, sharpest, most penetrating. Its holder (상쇠, sangsoe) leads the whole group with strokes, gestures, eye contact and shouts; covering the back of the gong with the left hand changes its pitch and damping
風物中才會出現。小鼓手邊打邊舞，太平簫提供旋律與遠距離訊號: Appears only in pungmul. The sogo player drums and dances at once, and the taepyeongso supplies melody and long-distance signals
風物是村落儀式與行列，包含旗、舞者、小鼓與太平簫，音樂服務於移動與祭祀；四物놀이: Pungmul is village ritual and procession, with flags, dancers, sogo and taepyeongso, and its music serves movement and offering; samul nori is the concert form that pulls the rhythms out and reorganises them for the stage. The two share their patterns but differ in line-up and purpose.
風物的一部分。隊伍的形狀與移動本身就是節奏的視覺版本: Part of pungmul. The shape and movement of the procession are a visual version of the rhythm
風物的節奏不是「一首曲子」，而是一組有名字的節奏型（장단），每一組有自己的速度、: The rhythm of pungmul is not "a piece" but a set of named patterns (장단, jangdan), each with its own tempo, number of beats and use. Players memorise the skeleton of the pattern and then decorate it. So two people playing the same pattern produce different details, but the skeleton must agree; that is why pungmul can carry a dozen people playing at once without falling apart.
風物與四物놀이 是同一件事，只是表演場地不同。: Pungmul and samul nori are the same thing, just performed in different places.
風物與農耕週期和村落祭祀綁在一起：正月的 달맞이、村落的 당산제、祈求豐收與驅厄: Pungmul is tied to the farming year and village ritual: the 달맞이 (dalmaji, moon greeting) in the first lunar month, the village 당산제 (dangsanje), rites asking for a good harvest and driving off misfortune, and the collective labour of the busy season. It is also an event in festivals and competitions, each region with its own style and group name. The route of the procession, its stopping places and the length of a performance are decided by ritual and local custom, not by a programme.
鼓負責讓所有人踩得到地。: The drum is what keeps everyone's feet on the ground.
